Oct 23 : FIFA President Gianni Infantino's reelection prospects have strengthened significantly after the head of Asian football endorsed his bid for a fourth term, leaving Europe increasingly isolated and exposing the lack of a credible challenger.
Asian Football Confederation President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa's endorsement, delivered at the AFC extraordinary congress in Tokyo on Friday, marked a striking reconciliation with Infantino.
Sheikh Salman had joined UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin and CONCACAF chief Victor Montagliani in criticising the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, which sought private investment in a new entity controlling commercial rights linked to major FIFA competitions, including the World Cup.
Their public opposition, followed by calls for Infantino to resign, raised questions about whether the FIFA president's previously solid support base was beginning to fracture.

But Sheikh Salman told the AFC's congress that Asia was united behind Infantino, two months after the confederation accused him of a "fundamental breach of trust" over the venture.
The turnaround has significantly narrowed the path for any challenger ahead of the March election.
ELECTORAL ARITHMETIC
Asia has 47 member associations, although only 46 are FIFA members eligible to vote in the presidential election. Each national federation has one vote in the FIFA election regardless of the country's size or its football pedigree.
Infantino had already secured support from Africa's 54-member confederation, where he has enjoyed strong relationships throughout his presidency.
South America's CONMEBOL has only 10 votes but did not join calls for his resignation, while most of Oceania's associations are also expected to remain in his camp.
CONCACAF, which represents North and Central America and the Caribbean, had initially joined UEFA and the AFC in criticising Infantino, but its member associations are now divided, with influential members including Mexico backing the incumbent.
Confederation endorsements do not formally bind individual associations, but the support available to Infantino across Asia, Africa and elsewhere gives him a commanding position among FIFA’s 211 voting members before nominations close on November 18.
That leaves UEFA, with its 55 associations, as the main centre of opposition, but even unanimous European support for another candidate would account for little more than a quarter of the electorate.
UEFA ISOLATED
UEFA has remained critical of Infantino and continues to seek answers regarding the abandoned FFE project and broader governance issues.
Europe, however, has not yet produced a credible challenger and is increasingly isolated in its opposition to Infantino, whose strength has always rested on building alliances beyond football's traditional power centres.
Sheikh Salman, Ceferin and Montagliani questioned both the substance of the FFE proposal and the way it had been presented.
Infantino subsequently abandoned the project and apologised over the way it had been handled at a closed FIFA Council meeting in Zurich last week.
The apology failed to sway European football associations but Sheikh Salman said in Tokyo that the two men had reached an understanding and should now "move forward".
Infantino's swift retreat and the promise of allocating $25 million to each association appear to have helped repair damaged relationships.
"In ten years since I became FIFA President, we have gone from $1 million per FIFA Member Association to $25 million each – all across the world," Infantino said.
"I would like to thank everyone who has made suggestions over the past few months on the distribution of FIFA's funds to our 211 FIFA Member Associations as we need to look forward in a spirit of unity and in the best interests of football."
Sheikh Salman's endorsement suggests the crisis that threatened to complicate Infantino's reelection campaign has so far cost him little lasting political support.
Unless UEFA can quickly produce a challenger capable of building support beyond Europe, the election increasingly looks less like a contest over Infantino's leadership than a demonstration of his continuing command of the electorate.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Roger Goodell: NFL targeting Tokyo for game in 2027 or 2028
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The NFL expects to be playing a regular-season game in Tokyo in either 2027 or 2028, commissioner Roger Goodell said on Friday.
items.body:
The NFL expects to be playing a regular-season game in Tokyo in either 2027 or 2028, commissioner Roger Goodell said on Friday.
"Listen, Tokyo is clearly on our list, whether it's next year or the year after. It's coming at some point in the near future," Goodell told NFL Daily.
"We're going to continue to focus on our priority markets, which a lot of them they've been in, but there are other cities; this year, we went to Rio (de Janeiro) rather than Sao Paulo.
Goodell was quick to point to the power of the NFL with its trip to Melbourne, Australia, for a Week 1 encounter between the San Francisco 49ers and rival Los Angeles Rams.
"On a Friday morning at 10:30 (a.m. local time), to have 100,000 people in the stadium, it was just an incredible feeling for us. I think it's opened up new opportunities for us," Goodell said. "The travel is something we think we can manage and do it without impacting negatively on the teams. So, each of these we learned something from and we benefit and we also open those other doors.
"We're planning on playing global. That's where we're going."
The NFL has played five of its nine international games thus far this season.
Goodell was in Paris on Friday in advance of the Pittsburgh Steelers' game on Sunday against the New Orleans Saints.
The league's second trip to Spain takes place in Week 9 with the Cincinnati Bengals battling the Atlanta Falcons on Nov. 8 in Madrid.
Next up is Germany, where the New England Patriots will meet the Detroit Lions in Week 10 on Nov. 15 in Munich.
The final international offering features the Minnesota Vikings and 49ers in Mexico City in Week 11 on Nov. 22
The NFL previously played 14 exhibition games in Japan, with the last one pitting the Falcons against the Indianapolis Colts in 2005.
--Field Level Media

items.title: POLL Bank of Canada to raise rates to 2.50% on October 28 and once again by end-March
items.author: Nushaiba Iqbal
items.creator: Nushaiba Iqbal
items.summary: The Bank of Canada will raise its overnight rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% on October 28 and follow with one more hike by the end of March to pre-empt any further rise in inflation expectations, according to a majority of economists polled by Reuters.
items.body:
The Bank of Canada will raise its overnight rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% on October 28 and follow with one more hike by the end of March to pre-empt any further rise in inflation expectations, according to a majority of economists polled by Reuters.
Inflation rose to [USN:L6N4620VU TEXT:"3.1%"] in September, only barely overshooting the BoC's target range of 1% to 3%. But the central bank's latest [USN:BCLJLEM2I TEXT:"business outlook survey"] showed sharply rising inflation expectations in the run-up to a recent breakdown in trade talks with the United States, Canada's main export destination.
Quarterly inflation forecasts from the bank, also due next week, are likely to be [USN:L6N463037 TEXT:"revised higher"], BoC Governor Tiff Macklem told reporters in remarks Saturday that markets interpreted as a hint a rate rise is coming.
Interest rate futures have moved from pricing in a 30% chance of a rate hike in October to around a three-in-four likelihood. Many economists this week changed their view from a hold to a hike, citing those remarks from Macklem.
"What changed the tone in the governor's public comments on the weekend and what changed our view on Monday is the same source, and that is the responses from the BoC's business outlook and consumer surveys," said Royce Mendes, managing director and head of macro strategy at Desjardins.
"So presumably the governor had seen the results before they were published more broadly on Monday. And I would assume that informed his public commentary," Mendes said. "The survey responses...suggest there are more serious inflationary pressures coming."
Nineteen of 34 economists surveyed in the October 21-23 poll, or 56% of them, said the BoC will hike its overnight rate by a quarter percentage point to 2.50%, its first move in a year.
This is a clear reversal from the previous poll, when 80% of respondents forecast the bank would hold its rate at 2.25% until the end of 2026, and two-thirds of them forecast a hold until the end of March 2027.
Those economists who forecast no move next week mainly cited a weak economy and subdued inflation pressures despite soaring oil prices , which hit $117 a barrel for the first time since May on Friday.
Sixteen of 29 respondents, a 55% majority, also forecast one more rise before March 2027, after which policymakers would hold the overnight rate at 2.75%, poll medians showed. If correct, it will be the shortest BoC policy tightening campaign in 30 years.
But even a short series of hikes would bring the BoC into a widening group of central banks that have opted for tighter monetary policy in response to persistent inflation emerging as a result of the US-led [USN:L6N46718Z TEXT:"war"] with Iran that began in February.
Among major central banks, only the BoC and the Bank of England — which is [USN:L6N4610Q9 TEXT:"widely expected"] to raise rates at its early November meeting — have not yet begun to raise rates.
But many say the BoC will need to be measured with the pace of rate increases given other risks to the economy.
Benjamin Reitzes, Canadian rates and macro strategist at BMO, said: "They'd rather make the mistake of hiking a little bit too early, which means maybe they have to hike a little bit less at the end of the day than falling behind the curve, which is what happened in 2021-2022, and they don't want to repeat that mistake.”
Economic growth likely slowed to 1.9% last quarter from 3.3% [USN:L6N44O17F TEXT:"in Q2"] and is forecast at 1.3% in the current one before accelerating next year, poll medians showed. The economy will grow 1.0% in 2026 and 1.7% in 2027, the survey found.
Inflation will average 2.8% for 2026 as a whole, falling to 2.3% in 2027, poll medians showed.
([USN:L6N45N0UX TEXT:"Other stories"] from the Reuters global economic poll)

＜ロンドン株式市場＞　まちまちで取引を終えた。英政府予算案の発表を来週に控え、積極的な買い注文が手控えられた。原油の値上がりも相場の重荷となり、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は続落。週間ベースでは１．７６％安と３週ぶりに反落した。一方、中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は前日比０．１１％上昇と反発、週間は１．２１％下落した。    ＦＴＳＥ３５０種石油・ガス株指数は前日比３．８８％上昇した。    一方、航空宇宙・防衛株指数は４．６４％下落。エンジンメーカーのロールスロイスは７．６％安だった。    銀行株指数は０．７８％、製薬・バイオテクノロジー株指数は１．０５％それぞれ下落。金価格の値下がりを受け、貴金属株指数は３．６５％値下がりした。    ９月の英小売売上高は前月から低下し、市場予想よりも低調だった。１０月の英消費者信頼感指数は大幅に悪化。物価動向を踏まえ、市場では１１月の英利上げが確実視されている。 

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞　続落して取引を終えた。フランスでの抗議活動や政局への不安のほか、原油高が相場の重荷となり、ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種指数は週間ベースでは１．３９％安と３週ぶりに反落した。    ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州高級品株１０種指数は前日比３．５９％安。フランスの高級ブランド、ケリングは１６．６％下落。中東情勢や中国での需要低迷が響き、主力ブランド、グッチの７─９月期の販売が減少した。一方、直近四半期決算の売上高が市場予想を上回ったフランスの化粧品大手ロレアルは５．６％上昇した。    ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種航空宇宙・防衛株指数は３．７５％安。決算を発表したフランスの航空機エンジンメーカーのサフランは１０．０％下落した。    直近四半期が営業赤字となったスウェーデンの自動車メーカー、ボルボ・カーは２４．２％安。約２５００人の人員削減計画を発表した。    欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）は来週、理事会を開く。市場では政策金利を据え置くとの観測が強い。 

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞　フランス国債利回り上昇が一服した。この日は、仏１０年国債利回りは５ｂｐ低下の５．０４％となった。    週間ベースでは２７ｂｐ近く上昇しており、２０２６年５月下旬以来の大幅な上昇を記録した。ベルギー国債利回りは１９ｂｐ近く、イタリア国債利回りも１１ｂｐ、それぞれ上昇した。これに対し、ドイツとオランダの１０年債利回りはそれぞれ７ｂｐ、６ｂｐ低下した。    ２３日は今週の流れが一部反転し、ドイツとオランダの利回りはともに２ｂｐ上昇し、それぞれ３．３５％、３．４６％となった。    来週は米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）、日銀、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）など主要中銀の金融政策決定が相次ぐ。    ＥＣＢは他の２中銀と同様、政策金利を据え置くと予想されている。このため投資家は、ラガルド総裁が見通しについて何を語るかに加え、フランス国債の緊張が市場の火種になり得るかどうかについての発言に注目することになる。    ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、短期金融市場は２３日、１２月までに利上げが行われる確率を再び約８０％に織り込んでいた。

items.body:
El presidente francés, Emmanuel Macron, calificó el tiroteo del viernes en Trappes, cerca de París, como un atentado terrorista y racista que ha marcado un punto de inflexión en la historia de Francia.
Macron afirmó que las víctimas del tirador de Trappes fueron elegidas como objetivo únicamente por su religión y el color de su piel.
"Lo ocurrido hoy marca un punto de inflexión para la República y para nuestro país. Lo ocurrido hoy ha sido un atentado terrorista y racista", declaró Macron a los periodistas el viernes.

items.title: Zelenskiy diz que negociadores ucranianos, russos e norte-americanos se reunirão no início de novembro em Abu Dhabi
items.author: Andrea Shalal, Olena Harmash
items.creator: Andrea Shalal, Olena Harmash
items.summary: O presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, disse nesta sexta-feira que os negociadores de paz da Ucrânia, da Rússia e dos Estados Unidos concordaram em se reunir em nível técnico na primeira quinzena de novembro, em Abu Dhabi, acrescentando que espera que isso seja seguido por um encontro entre os líderes desses países.
items.body:
O presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, disse nesta sexta-feira que os negociadores de paz da Ucrânia, da Rússia e dos Estados Unidos concordaram em se reunir em nível técnico na primeira quinzena de novembro, em Abu Dhabi, acrescentando que espera que isso seja seguido por um encontro entre os líderes desses países.
Zelenskiy disse ter conversado com os enviados dos EUA, Jared Kushner e Steve Witkoff, nesta sexta-feira, após a reunião deles com o presidente da Rússia, Vladimir Putin, no início desta semana. Ele afirmou que qualquer acordo de paz precisará de fortes garantias de segurança para a Ucrânia e de financiamento por 10 anos para manter o Exército ucraniano.
“O plano é nos reunirmos na primeira quinzena de novembro e, o mais cedo possível, é claro”, disse Zelenskiy ao think tank Hudson Institute por meio de uma videoconferência. Ele afirmou que muito dependeria da Rússia, observando que uma reunião semelhante prevista para este mês não havia se concretizado.
Zelenskiy enfatizou a importância de esforços diplomáticos contínuos para alcançar um cessar-fogo e pôr fim à guerra, que já está em seu quinto ano, acrescentando que a Europa também deveria participar das negociações.
O presidente ucraniano disse que é fundamental que as discussões técnicas sejam seguidas por uma reunião dos líderes dos países.
(Reportagem de Andrea Shalal)

items.title: イラン、海底ケーブル攻撃準備　米・イスラエル再攻撃なら＝治安高官
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ドバイ　２３日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[ドバイ　２３日　ロイター] - 米国とイスラエルがイランを再び攻撃した場合、イランがペルシャ湾の海底通信ケーブルを標的とする攻撃の詳細な計画を策定していることがイラン治安当局高官２人の話で分かった。

イラン当局者はこれまでも、米国との外交交渉が決裂し新たな戦闘が発生すれば、海底ケーブルが攻撃対象になり得ると警告。匿名を条件に取材に応じた２人の高官は、攻撃の具体的な手法や実施場所について明らかにしなかったが、このうち１人は、インターネット接続を含む通信の混乱を長期化させるため、攻撃後の修復作業を妨害することを目指す考えを示した。

同高官はロイターに対し「イランが攻撃されれば、もはやレッドライン（越えてはならない一線）は存在しない。海底ケーブルから軍事基地まで、秘密基地も含めて標的になり得る」と指摘。米国は「火遊びをしてはならない」とし、イランは海底ケーブルの位置を完全に把握しており、容易に破壊できると主張した。

海底ケーブルを巡っては、イランのイスラム革命防衛隊（ＩＲＧＣ）のジャバニ政治担当副司令官が２１日、イランのインフラが攻撃を受けた場合、ホルムズ海峡の海底に敷設された主要なインターネット通信ケーブル７本を標的にする可能性があると述べている。

国連機関の国際電気通信連合（ＩＴＵ）によると、海底ケーブルは世界のインターネット通信量の約９９％を担っている。ただ、通信調査会社テレジオグラフィーの調査責任者アラン・モールディン氏は、ホルムズ海峡を通過する国際通信帯域は全体の１％未満にとどまるため、イランによる攻撃があっても世界全体に及ぶ影響は限定される可能性があると指摘している。

イラン治安当局高官の発言について、米国務省とイラン外務省からコメントは得られていない。湾岸諸国も現時点でコメントしていない。

items.title: Mark Cuban says AI hack agents are like cockroaches, but can be controlled
items.author: Caroline Humer
items.creator: Caroline Humer
items.summary: Billionaire entrepreneur Mark Cuban said on Friday that he is "not a doomer" about artificial intelligence and that companies should be able to use the technology to protect themselves from AI-driven hacks by agents that he compared to cockroaches.
items.body:
Billionaire entrepreneur Mark Cuban said on Friday that he is "not a doomer" about artificial intelligence and that companies should be able to use the technology to protect themselves from AI-driven hacks by agents that he compared to cockroaches.
"It's like the cockroach thing, right? You build a new house, you get the guys to come out and spray... the one thing I don't want is cockroaches in my house ever. But the cockroaches find a way to get in because there's zillions of them, right? And then if there's one gets in, there's more that are going to get in, and that's kind of the way AI works," Cuban said, speaking at Reuters Total Health.
"It's all brute force acts, and if it's brute force on that side with the bad guys, you can also use brute force with the good guys," he said.
Cuban, famous for his role on business reality show "Shark Tank" and his involvement in the Dallas Mavericks NBA team, ventured into healthcare when he started the online pharmacy Cost Plus Drug Company in 2022 with a standard pricing scheme: the cost it pays for the drug, plus 15%.
In May, Cost Plus signed on with TrumpRx.gov, a website created by the Trump administration selling discounted weight-loss drugs.
But the company has also moved into manufacturing. In 2025, it began making sterile injectable drugs typically used in hospitals in its own compounding manufacturing facility.
Cuban said the company has built smaller, tractor-trailer-sized manufacturing facilities he calls "pods" that can be used separately or together to manufacture many kinds of drugs, including generics and treatments for rare diseases.
He said the pods would eventually be Cost Plus Drugs' biggest business and would allow medicines to be manufactured closer to where they are needed in the event of a disaster, because they're portable.
One holdup, Cuban said, has been getting regulators from the US Food and Drug Administration to sign off on the pods.
"We're talking to the FDA to try to get approval," he said without outlining the complications. "They're working hard to try to figure it out."
Cuban campaigned for Democratic presidential nominee Kamala Harris in 2024 and has supported Democratic candidate James Talarico for US Senate this year in Texas.
He said two items he believes the US government should immediately put in place to help lower healthcare costs would be that all payments made out of pocket should count towards patients' deductibles and that taxpayer-funded health contracts should be public without redactions.
Still, Cuban said he did not believe Democrats were necessarily better than Republicans on healthcare.
"None of them know what they're doing," he said.

items.title: Knicks signing Dalton Knecht to a 2-way contract
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The New York Knicks are signing former first-round draft pick Dalton Knecht to a two-way deal.
items.body:
The New York Knicks are signing former first-round draft pick Dalton Knecht to a two-way deal.
The 25-year-old forward's agents with Excel Sports Management confirmed the move to ESPN on Friday.
The Los Angeles Lakers selected Knecht, known in college at Tennessee as a sharpshooter, with the No. 17 overall pick of the 2024 NBA Draft. He fell out of the rotation last season and the Lakers waived him earlier this week.
As a 2024-25 rookie in 78 games, Knecht averaged 9.1 points and 2.8 rebounds over 19.2 minutes per game, shooting 37.6% from 3-point range. Last season, his productivity (4.2 points, 1.4 rebounds) and minutes (10.2) were cut by about half.
The Knicks will waive forward Kevin McCullar Jr., who currently occupies a two-way spot, to make room for Knecht, multiple outlets reported Friday.
--Field Level Media

items.title: NFL closes Paris pop-up shop ahead of planned protests
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The NFL will close its Paris pop-up shop on Saturday because of planned demonstrations in the French capital ahead of this weekend's regular-season game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints, the league said on Friday.
items.body:
The NFL will close its Paris pop-up shop on Saturday because of planned demonstrations in the French capital ahead of [USN:L1N4690K8 TEXT:"this weekend's regular-season game"] between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints, the league said on Friday.
The store on Rue Saint-Merri had been operating as part of events surrounding Sunday's game at the Stade de France, the first NFL regular-season contest to be held in France.
"The NFL Shop on Rue Saint-Merri will be closed tomorrow Saturday 24 October, due to potential accessibility issues," the league said in a statement.
The street is located in Paris' fourth arrondissement, in the city centre.
The league said the shop would remain open until 8 p.m. local time on Friday and that an alternative NFL pop-up store would operate at the Stade de France on Saturday.
The Steelers had already cancelled a fan event scheduled for the weekend at a bar on Place de la Bastille amid concerns over the demonstrations.
France experienced some of its worst urban unrest in recent years last weekend, prompting President Emmanuel Macron's government to tighten restrictions on protests as authorities prepared for the possibility of further violence on Saturday.
Sunday's game will take place in Saint-Denis, about 10 km north of Paris centre, with organisers continuing preparations despite disruption elsewhere in the city.
Concerns over renewed unrest have also led several major cultural venues, including the Louvre, to close on Saturday, while the Art Basel Paris fair will remain shut throughout the weekend.

items.title: Paris looting image misidentifies woman as store owner
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: A video of a woman confronting masked individuals at a Paris grocery shop entrance has been mischaracterised online with unfounded details of it showing a pro-asylum activist trying to stop her boutique from being looted by the refugees she supports.
items.body:
A video of a woman confronting masked individuals at a Paris grocery shop entrance has been mischaracterised online with unfounded details of it showing a pro-asylum activist trying to stop her boutique from being looted by the refugees she supports.
The posts , from mid-October, shared an image of a woman in a doorway with her arms outstretched, with people wearing face coverings nearby.
The posts don't refer to the woman by name, though they claim she's a member of a French left-wing party and is famous for her activism in "defending North African refugees".
“She owns a small chic boutique in an upscale spot, she stood in her shop trying to save it from looting and theft,” the posts said.
They added that the looters "spat on her, knocked her down, and trampled her with their feet", despite the woman identifying herself and saying she was the "activist for asylum" who supported their entries and stays in France.
Reuters has not identified the woman or the people wearing face coverings.
However, the image is a cropped and edited screenshot from a video that contradicts parts of the posts, such as showing the woman in front of a consortium-owned convenience store chain rather than a boutique.
The screenshot, which has been edited to remove graffiti from the storefront, was taken from an Instagram video posted by Paris-based photojournalist Frederic Munsch.
The video shows the woman stepping into the doorway of a Franprix shop in Paris and shouting "Stop!", “Why are you doing this?” and “That’s not what the cause is about!” as masked individuals push past her into the store.
Masked individuals can also be seen exiting the shop with handfuls of goods, while later shots show a smashed window and ransacked aisles inside.
The woman does not introduce herself by name or mention asylum activism. She is pulled aside in the video by another person wearing a face covering and, seconds later, appears to step away.
The video does not show the woman being knocked down and trampled.
Franprix is a convenience store chain and part of French supermarket group Plesio , formerly Casino, owned by Czech billionaire [USN:S8N3RE0BD TEXT:"Daniel Kretinsky"].
There are more than a thousand Franprix stores in France, according to the Plesio website .
Plesio’s communications department told Reuters in an email that the store in the video, situated on Rue du Faubourg du Temple, is company-owned and operated, and that the woman is not an employee.
Munsch told Reuters via email that he filmed the video on October 17 at approximately 5:30 p.m. local time.
He said he did not personally know the woman, though he said he believed she had been "passing by".
Cost-of-living [USN:S8N42Q0F9 TEXT:"protests"] that day at the nearby Place de la Republique and in other French cities deteriorated into rioting and looting and later turned into some of the country's worst urban unrest in years.
VERDICT Misleading. The video from which the image was taken shows the woman standing in the doorway of a Franprix convenience store branch, not a boutique, and the store's owners said the woman is not an employee. The posts offer no evidence for their claims about the woman's identity or the things they cite her as saying.
This article was produced by the Reuters Fact Check team. Read more about our fact-checking work.

items.title: トランプ氏、カナダ産農林業製品の一部関税撤廃　中間選挙控え国境州に配慮
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ワシントン　２３日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[ワシントン　２３日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２３日、一部のカナダ産農林業製品に対する５０％関税を撤廃する大統領令に署名した。中間選挙を前にメイン州選出の共和党議員の要請を受けたもので、米農業関連企業の負担軽減につながる可能性がある。

今回の措置は、厳しい再選戦を戦っているメイン州選出のスーザン・コリンズ上院議員（共和党）が同州の企業や農家に影響を及ぼしている関税問題への対応をホワイトハウスに求めたことを受けたもの。ホワイトハウスによると、合板、一部の紙製品、特定の機械や冷却設備、梱包用の木箱や容器などが関税撤廃の対象になる。

トランプ氏は８月、カナダとの関税協議が決裂したことを受け、カナダからの２００億ドル相当の輸入品に対し５０％の関税を課すと発表していた。

コリンズ議員は、今回の措置でメイン州のブルーベリー、ジャガイモ、リンゴ、海藻の生産者が恩恵を受けると指摘。声明で「これらの生産者は州経済にとって不可欠な存在で、地方や沿岸部の地域社会を支えている」とし、「多くの農家や生産業者はカナダから調達する特殊な機械や包装資材などに依存している。こうした製品は米国内では入手できない場合があるほか、代替には多額の費用がかかる」とした。

カナダとの国境に近い米北部のメイン州やミシガン州などは関税措置の影響を大きく受けており、１１月３日の中間選挙に向け一部の共和党候補は難しい対応を迫られている。特にメイン州とミシガン州の経済は自動車部品や木材、果実収穫用機器など幅広い分野でカナダ経済と深く結び付いており、関税政策を巡る政治的な重要性が一段と高まっている。

items.title: Chili's workers' lawsuit looks to strike New York state's lower wage for tipped workers
items.author: Daniel Wiessner
items.creator: Daniel Wiessner
items.summary: A lawsuit filed on Friday involving the pay practices of Chili's operator Brinker International is seeking to strike down New York state's lower minimum wage for workers who earn tips, which it claims fuels the sexual and racial harassment of workers.
items.body:
A lawsuit filed on Friday involving the pay practices of Chili's operator Brinker International (EAT.N) is seeking to strike down New York state's lower minimum wage for workers who earn tips, which it claims fuels the sexual and racial harassment of workers.
The proposed class action in federal court in Brooklyn by three former Chili's employees claims that New York's policy, which most other US states share, allows Brinker to force employees to rely on tips and exposes them to unlawful discrimination.
"Brinker promotes a culture in which tipped service employees make customers 'feel special,' even at the expense of their dignity and safety," the lawsuit says.
Brinker did not respond to a request for comment. The New York Attorney General's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the challenge to the state law.
Many worker advocates have for years called for the [USN:L1N3MD0Y5 TEXT:"elimination of sub-minimum wages"] that companies may pay to workers who earn tips under federal and most state laws, as long as tips make up the difference.
In New York, where the minimum wage is $16 an hour or $17 in and around New York City, food service workers who earn tips may be paid $10.70 or $11.35 an hour. The federal tipped minimum wage is $2.13 an hour, compared with the traditional minimum wage of $7.25, and applies in states that do not set their own minimums.
RELYING ON TIPS Advocates say that because tips are discretionary and unpredictable, they should supplement workers' incomes rather than make up most of their pay. The lawsuit against Brinker says that relying on tips forces workers to tolerate conduct such as sexual harassment and customers' potential racial bias.
The plaintiffs' lawyers said in the lawsuit that they plan to expand the case to include a nationwide class of Chili's workers.
Brinker operates more than 1,200 Chili's restaurants in the US, including 36 in New York. The company also owns Maggiano's Little Italy, an Italian restaurant chain with about 50 US locations.
The lawsuit claims that Chili's reliance on customer ratings to determine workers' schedules, shifts and table assignments is also unlawful. The ratings system can be racially biased, the lawsuit says, and can make it difficult for servers to reject unwanted advances from customers for fear of a poor rating.
The named plaintiffs, three former employees at a Chili's in the Glendale section of Queens in New York City, claim they were routinely subjected to sexual advances and inappropriate comments and that management did not adequately protect workers from harassment.

WASHINGTON, Oct 23 : US Senator Marsha Blackburn, a Tennessee Republican, on Friday raised concerns about Facebook parent Meta Platforms' plan to update its commercial terms, saying it could harm businesses and creators.
Blackburn, who is chair of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Privacy, Technology and the Law, said the updated terms "indicate Meta is attempting to exploit American creators and businesses by granting itself sweeping authority to scrape content from any website associated with Facebook and Instagram business accounts." 
Earlier on Friday, Meta said it would delay the implementation of updated commercial terms from October 30 until November 20, so it can address concerns from publishers and digital advertisers.
EU and UK antitrust authorities have received complaints about the new commercial terms, which publishers and digital advertisers said would give Meta unlimited rights to use their content for its AI services. Meta has rejected the claims.

Blackburn said that Meta previously revised its terms to remove an explicit reference to AI training but said the changes did not go far enough. She added that the revised language authorizes extensive scraping of external websites and permits Meta to “develop” its business products with collected content.
"Without clear restrictions on how that information may be used, including whether it may be incorporated into AI systems, Meta’s revisions offer little assurance that creators’ intellectual property will be protected," Blackburn said. She added: "This is particularly troubling for American news publishers, creators, and small businesses that rely on Meta’s platforms to reach their audiences and customers."
Asked for comment on Blackburn's letter, Meta on Friday noted it had delayed the change and said the revised terms apply only to its ads and business products and that it is not changing how it uses web crawlers.
"These updates don't give us new rights to supersede such preferences and this isn’t about scraping news sites," the company said, noting that "content owners will still be able to use robots.txt to signal preferences."
Publishers worldwide are ramping up fights with AI companies using their content without permission to train large language models, underscoring the clash between copyright owners and those citing fair-use arguments.
"Meta must withdraw the updated Commercial Terms and come to the table to protect the content of creators and publishers across the country," Blackburn said. "American creators and small businesses are not a free source of content for Meta to exploit."

Source: Reuters

items.title: Sebi orders Avadhut Sathe Trading Academy and its founder to refund ₹546 cr
items.author: Press Trust of India
items.summary: The regulator has also barred the academy and Sathe from accessing the securities market for two years or until compliance with the refund direction, whichever is later ...
items.body: Markets regulator Sebi on Friday directed Avadhut Sathe Trading Academy Pvt Ltd (ASTAPL) and its Founder Avadhut Sathe to refund Rs 546.17 crore collected from participants for providing unregistered investment advisory and research analyst services, along with interest of Rs 67.87 crore.The regulator has also barred the academy and Sathe from accessing the securities market for two years or until compliance with the refund direction, whichever is later.In its 171-page final order, the regulator imposed a total penalty of Rs 11.5 crore on the academy, Sathe and Gouri Avadhut Sathe for violations of securities market regulations.The academy has been fined Rs 6 crore, Sathe has been fined Rs 4 crore, while Gouri Avadhut Sathe has been penalised Rs 1.5 crore.The regulator found that the academy and Sathe provided investment advice and research recommendations through paid programmes, sessions and WhatsApp groups without obtaining the required registration.It also found that misleading promotional representations about returns were used to attract participants and that investment advice was provided without assessing the suitability of recommendations for recipients.The order said the academy and Sathe had collected around Rs 601.38 crore from course participants since inception. However, based on the evidence examined, fees of Rs 546.17 crore attributable to the relevant programmes were identified for disgorgement and refund.Sebi has directed the academy and Sathe to complete the refunds within five months of receiving the order. They have also been asked to publish notices in newspapers within 30 days, explaining the procedure for investors to claim refunds.The regulator has further directed that their bank accounts remain frozen for debits until the required amounts are deposited into the designated account and Sebi's Investor Protection and Education Fund, as applicable.Gouri Avadhut Sathe has been barred from accessing the securities market for six months. Sebi said her liability arose from a failure to exercise oversight.

items.title: Top LNG exporter QatarEnergy in talks to buy US LNG from Woodside's Louisiana plant
items.author: Curtis Williams, Marwa Rashad
items.creator: Curtis Williams, Marwa Rashad
items.summary: QatarEnergy is in talks with Woodside Energy to buy up to 3 million metric tons of liquefied natural gas per annum (mtpa) from its Louisiana LNG plant under construction, three people with knowledge of the negotiations told Reuters.
items.body:
QatarEnergy is in talks with Woodside Energy (WDS.AX) to buy up to 3 million metric tons of liquefied natural gas per annum (mtpa) from its Louisiana LNG plant under construction, three people with knowledge of the negotiations told Reuters.
If a final agreement is reached, the long-term deal could see QatarEnergy buying LNG from the 16.5 mtpa export facility for between 15 and 20 years, one of the people said.
Woodside Energy said on Friday it does not respond to market speculation, while QatarEnergy did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
QatarEnergy has been buying LNG on the spot market from US exporters to supply some of its customers due to the ongoing blockage of the Strait of Hormuz as the US-Israeli war on Iran and Tehran’s strikes this year have sharply curtailed shipping.
The company is also a 70% owner of the Golden Pass LNG facility being developed in Louisiana, which when complete will have the capacity to export up to 18 mtpa of LNG.
On Thursday, Cheniere Energy (LNG.N) reported it had reached a long-term agreement to supply QatarEnergy with 4 mtpa of LNG. Two million metric tons per year will be sourced from Cheniere’s Sabine Pass facility in Louisiana, and another 2 mpta will come from its Corpus Christi terminal in Texas.
Reuters also [USN:L1N468185 TEXT:"reported"] on Thursday that QatarEnergy is in advanced talks with Venture Global (VG.N) for a long-term supply deal to buy at least 3 million metric tons of LNG per year.
Venture Global and Woodside's Louisiana LNG are the US suppliers with the most uncommitted LNG capacity.
Louisiana LNG is said to be asking for a premium for liquefaction fees that exceed $2.50 per mmBtu and are above the average US market prices because of contract flexibility, offering potential buyers shorter contracts in return for higher prices, two people told Reuters.

items.title: Trump removes 50% tariffs on Canadian products to try to boost to Maine companies
items.author: David Shepardson
items.creator: David Shepardson
items.summary: President Donald Trump on Friday signed an order to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products, which could boost US agriculture firms dependent on those goods.
items.body:
President Donald Trump on Friday signed an order to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products, which could boost US agriculture firms dependent on those goods.
The move came after Maine Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is facing a tough re-election bid, urged the White House to address tariffs on products affecting Maine companies and farmers. Republican candidates in northern US border states most affected by the tariffs, including Maine and Michigan, are trying to strike a balance between appealing to Trump’s loyal base and winning over independent voters.
Trump is exempting plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment, and packing crates and boxes, the White House said. Collins said the relief will aid the state's blueberry, potato, apple, and seaweed producers.
“These producers are a vital part of our state’s economy and support our rural and coastal communities," Collins said. "Many of our farmers and growers rely on specialized equipment, packaging materials, and other products from Canada that are ether unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense."
Collins clashed with her opponent, Democrat Troy Jackson, over the subject of tariffs at an October 6 debate.
Trump in August imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian imports, which took effect after talks between the two countries collapsed in August. The two have been locked in a standoff since then, though Trump on Friday asserted that Canada is working on a deal.
The administration is adding certain valves, carpets, waste products, and other items to the list, the White House said.
The economies of Michigan and Maine have long been intertwined with Canada’s, covering everything from auto parts to lumber to fruit-picking equipment. That has raised the stakes in two states that Republicans will likely need to win in the November 3 elections if they are to hold the US Senate.

items.title: Bills' Sam Franklin Jr. wins appeal, suspension reduced to fine
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Buffalo Bills safety and special teams captain Sam Franklin Jr. won his appeal to overturn the one-game suspension he initially received from the NFL for allegedly spitting at an opponent.
items.body:
Buffalo Bills safety and special teams captain Sam Franklin Jr. won his appeal to overturn the one-game suspension he initially received from the NFL for allegedly spitting at an opponent.
The league announced Friday that it reduced the punishment to a fine of $14,926 for unsportsmanlike conduct. Franklin will be allowed to play in Week 8 when the Bills return from their bye to face the Baltimore Ravens on Nov. 1.
Fellow Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was not as fortunate. His suspension for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers was upheld upon appeal on Thursday. He will be eligible to return to the active roster on Nov. 2.
Per a release on Wednesday, the NFL said Franklin spat at an opposing player after Las Vegas made an extra point with 1:32 left in the fourth quarter.
Franklin denied that he spat at a player and even posted a video clip to his Instagram account showing the extra-point play in slow motion. The clip cut off before the play ends.
"Not a dirty play what so ever!" Franklin captioned the video clip. "Will always defend myself though. Still won't spit on anyone."
His agents, Harold C. Lewis and Christian Addison, said in a statement that they "adamantly deny" Franklin spit at anyone.
Franklin, 30, has recorded six tackles on special teams in six games this season. He has 124 tackles and a 99-yard interception return for a touchdown in 97 career games (nine starts) with the Carolina Panthers (2020-24) and Bills.
--Field Level Media

items.title: “Íris”, de Claude Monet, torna-se obra de arte mais cara já vendida em leilão na França, diz Sotheby’s
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A obra “Íris”, de Claude Monet, foi vendida na noite de quinta-feira por 50 milhões de euros (56,05 milhões de dólares), tornando-se a obra de arte mais cara já vendida em leilão na França, informou a Sotheby’s.
items.body:
A obra “Íris”, de Claude Monet, foi vendida na noite de quinta-feira por 50 milhões de euros (56,05 milhões de dólares), tornando-se a obra de arte mais cara já vendida em leilão na França, informou a Sotheby’s.
A pintura, concluída no final da vida de Monet, atraiu uma disputa acirrada, com seis pessoas disputando a obra por 45 minutos, antes que dois finalistas continuassem a disputa por mais 20 minutos.
“Íris” acabou indo para um colecionador asiático que fez a oferta por telefone.
A pintura era uma das várias obras da Coleção Schlumberger colocadas à venda no leilão e esperava-se que fosse vendida por um valor entre 22 milhões e 30 milhões de euros.
O recorde anterior em leilões na França havia sido estabelecido em 2010, com a obra “Cabeça de uma Cariátide”, de Amedeo Modigliani, vendida por 43,2 milhões de euros.
(Reportagem de Makini Brice)

By Makini Brice and Crispian Balmer
PARIS, Oct 23 (Reuters) – France will deploy 70,000 police at nationwide protests on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Friday, looking to prevent a repeat of the violence and looting that shocked the country last weekend.

Elite security teams and heavily armed mobile squads will be mobilised alongside regular units in a show of force aimed at dispelling fears the government has lost control of the streets.

“We will be uncompromising with rioters, looters and all those who commit acts of violence,” Nunez told reporters, adding that “ultra-left” groups had been urging activists online to target public buildings and unleash more lawlessness.

Show Full Article

“We are not talking about a nice, friendly demonstration,” Nunez said. “We are ready for tomorrow. We will be extremely vigilant, extremely firm, and we will let absolutely nothing pass.”

SHOOTING SPREE NEAR PARIS ADDS TO TENSIONS

Anger over living costs and strained public services has drawn students, workers and unions onto the streets in recent weeks, but authorities say radical militants and bands of young looters have taken advantage of the dispute to sow chaos.

Some far-right politicians have blamed migrants and radical Islam for the turmoil. President Emmanuel Macron has dismissed such accusations.

Ratcheting up the tensions, a man, who officials suspect was motivated by Islamophobic hatred, opened fire from a car west of Paris on Friday, killing one person and wounding four others, including a 12-year-old girl.

“(It was) objectively a racist attack,” said local mayor Ali Rabeh, blaming far-right rhetoric for inflaming tensions.

Police have authorised only one union demonstration in Paris on Saturday, rejecting requests for rallies lodged by France’s main student union, UNEF, and the Yellow Vest movement, an anti-establishment force that first emerged in 2018.

Many French cities beyond Paris have also banned protests but the second largest city, Marseille, rescinded an earlier restriction order and said it would allow a union demonstration.

UNEF said its rallies, which grew from high school protests last month against teacher shortages and shabby facilities, would go ahead regardless.

Marylise Leon, the general secretary of the CFDT, one of the nation’s largest trade unions, criticised Macron for not sanctioning more demonstrations.

“It’s counterproductive because there is a lot of anger, a lot of anger and a demand to be considered and to be listened to,” she told French broadcaster TF1. “It’s not for the president to decide who can legitimately request to protest.”

FAR-RIGHT CONGRESS A POSSIBLE FLASHPOINT

Nunez said 10,000 more police would be on the streets than a week ago, while mounted police, helicopters, drones and anti-drone systems would be deployed across the country.

Armoured vehicles and water cannon vehicles would also be available, while curfews imposed in some sensitive areas this past week would remain in force.

Authorities are also concerned that the annual congress of Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally in Orleans this weekend could become a flashpoint, with left-wing and anti-racist groups announcing counter-demonstrations.

The upsurge of violence has boosted poll ratings for Le Pen, who is the frontrunner for next year’s presidential election. She has portrayed the unrest as evidence of a collapse in state authority.

Fears of renewed turmoil prompted several of Paris’ best-known cultural institutions, including the Louvre, the Musée d’Orsay and the Opera House, to close all day on Saturday.

Paris St Germain’s home Ligue 1 soccer match with Olympique Lyonnais was shifted from Sunday to Monday over security concerns. However, an NFL regular-season game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints is still scheduled to be played in Paris on Sunday, although US President Donald Trump suggested it should be cancelled.

Business groups also urged shops to stay shut after some 3,000 stores and businesses were ransacked last weekend.

Alain Di Crescenzo, the president of France’s chamber of commerce, said some shopkeepers were arming themselves with baseball bats, crowbars and shotguns to protect their properties. But he urged them not to turn to violence.

“It’s extremely worrying,” he told Europe 1 radio. “It’s not their job to do that. It would add suffering onto suffering.”

The social turbulence has intensified scrutiny of France’s economic outlook and ratings agency Moody’s is widely expected to cut the French credit rating on Friday, underscoring concern that the government had not reined in public spending.

items.title: Packers LB Zaire Franklin out Sunday with shin injury
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin will miss Sunday's game at Detroit with a shin injury sustained in Thursday's practice.
items.body:
Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin will miss Sunday's game at Detroit with a shin injury sustained in Thursday's practice.
"Unfortunately, Zaire, there was a little collision -- he got kneed in the shin," head coach Matt LaFleur said Friday. "So, he's going to be out this game."
Franklin, 30, ranks second on the Packers (4-2) with 41 tackles through his first six starts with the team.
"I don't think it's going to be anything too long-term," LaFleur added. "But, yeah, just (an) unfortunate deal. That happens when you play football, especially the way our guys have been practicing."
Acquired in a March trade with Indianapolis, Franklin played his first eight NFL seasons with the Colts and made the Pro Bowl in 2024. The 2018 seventh-round draft pick has 779 tackles, 10 sacks, 11 forced fumbles and three interceptions in 138 career games (88 starts).
Franklin's absence means more playing time for Ty'Ron Hopper and Isaiah McDuffie against the NFC North rival Lions (3-2).
"I think we've got a lot of confidence in McDuffie, and Hopper, and Nick Niemann if need be, to go in there and do a great job for us," LaFleur said.
--Field Level Media

items.title: França investiga suposto tiroteio islamofóbico contra menina perto de Paris como ato de terrorismo
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Um atirador, que as autoridades suspeitam ter sido motivado por ódio islamofóbico, abriu fogo de um carro nesta sexta-feira, a oeste de Paris, matando uma pessoa e ferindo outras quatro, incluindo uma menina de 12 anos.
items.body:
Um atirador, que as autoridades suspeitam ter sido motivado por ódio islamofóbico, abriu fogo de um carro nesta sexta-feira, a oeste de Paris, matando uma pessoa e ferindo outras quatro, incluindo uma menina de 12 anos.
“As investigações estão em andamento, mas trata-se claramente de um crime terrorista. É um ato extremamente grave”, disse o ministro do Interior, Laurent Nuñez, a repórteres no distrito de Yvelines, a oeste de Paris, onde ocorreu o ataque.
Autoridades informaram que o suspeito de 39 anos, cujo nome não foi divulgado, dirigiu pela cidade de Trappes, onde disparou uma arma automática contra um posto de gasolina, um centro médico e um parque infantil.
A emissora BFM informou que a menina ferida foi atingida oito vezes e estava em estado grave.
“(Foi) objetivamente um ataque racista, provavelmente islamofóbico”, disse Ali Rabeh, prefeito de Trappes, cujos pais são originários de Marrocos. “As pessoas atacadas hoje poderiam muito bem ter sido minha mãe, meus irmãos ou minhas cunhadas.”
A polícia conseguiu prender o homem antes que ele pudesse ferir mais alguém. Imagens de vídeo mostraram seu carro crivado de balas.
O tiroteio ocorre em um momento de tensão especial na França, depois que protestos em todo o país se tornaram violentos no último sábado e antes de novas manifestações previstas para o fim de semana.
Alguns políticos de extrema direita atribuíram à imigração a onda de saques e vandalismo que assolou várias cidades francesas em 17 de outubro.
Rabeh, que é um político de esquerda, pediu uma condenação coletiva da retórica que “arma ideologicamente aqueles capazes de cometer tais atos”.
A Promotoria Antiterrorismo, conhecida como PNAT, informou que sua investigação inclui a análise de se o tiroteio teve motivação racial ou religiosa.
A PNAT pode assumir qualquer investigação criminal que considere atender aos critérios de terrorismo, incluindo violência inspirada por ideias de extrema direita. As penas por terrorismo são mais severas, e as forças antiterroristas têm maiores poderes de investigação.
Nicolas Dainville, prefeito da vizinha La Verrière, disse que o suspeito morava na cidade de Plaisir, também no departamento de Yvelines, e era “de aparência europeia”. Rabeh afirmou que duas das vítimas eram de origem africana e norte-africana, respectivamente, e não forneceu detalhes sobre as origens das demais vítimas.
(Reportagem de Juliette Jabkhiro, Dominique Vidalon, Zhifan Liu e Sudip Kar-Gupta)

items.title: Loblaw says March data breach affected about two million Canadians
items.author: The Canadian Press
items.summary: Loblaw says it is starting to notify about two million Canadians who were affected by a data breach in March with specifics about which personal information of theirs leaked.
items.body: BRAMPTON — Loblaw says it is starting to notify about two million Canadians who were affected by a data breach in March with specifics about which personal information of theirs leaked. The grocer is notifying affected consumers directly about the breach, which may have revealed data including their name, email address, home address, date of birth, loyalty card number, certain purchase order details and partial payment card information. Although, it says the extent of the leak is different for everyone and not all types of information were involved for every customer. Loblaw is also advising customers on next steps and asking them to beware of unexpected emails, calls or texts. It is offering complimentary credit monitoring and identity restoration services through TransUnion. The company said in March that it detected suspicious activity on its IT network and determined an unauthorized third party had accessed some basic customer information but didn’t disclose how many customers were affected at the time. It said it conducted a detailed investigation, notified law enforcement and regulatory authorities, and strengthened its security systems. This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 23, 2026.

items.title: Novartis presents weaker-than-expected relapse data for multiple sclerosis drug remibrutinib
items.author: Bhanvi Satija, Marleen Kaesebier
items.creator: Bhanvi Satija, Marleen Kaesebier
items.summary: Swiss drugmaker Novartis' oral multiple sclerosis (MS) drug remibrutinib meaningfully reduced relapses in patients, according to data presented at a medical conference in Toronto on Friday, but less than analysts had expected.
items.body:
Swiss drugmaker Novartis' (NOVN.S) oral multiple sclerosis (MS) drug remibrutinib meaningfully reduced relapses in patients, according to data presented at a medical conference in Toronto on Friday, but less than analysts had expected.
The drug reduced annualized relapse rates by 35.2% and 31.2%, compared with teriflunomide, an older MS treatment sold by Sanofi under the brand name Aubagio. Analysts had expected a reduction of 45% to 60%.
The detailed trial results, previously disclosed only in top-line form, were presented days after Roche (ROPC.S) released its own data on [USN:L6N4660XX TEXT:"rival MS drug"] fenebrutinib. In pooled Phase III data, Roche reported a 55% reduction in annualized relapse rate versus teriflunomide.
"All in all, they might be quite similar in what they do in terms of reducing relapses and disability," Heinz Wiendl, co-chair of the Novartis studies, said in an interview.
Ahead of the readout, analysts said that relapse improvements similar to those seen in Roche's trial would be needed to show that this class of treatments is better than the currently used anti-CD20 therapies. These include Ocrevus, Novartis' Kesimpta and TG Therapeutics' (TGTX.O) Briumvi, which target and kill the immune cells that drive MS.
Novartis is banking on the success of the drug across different therapeutic areas, especially following a string of [USN:L4N4510T5 TEXT:"recent trial setbacks"] for its heart drug pelacarsen and muscle weakness therapy del-desiran.
Analysts currently estimate remibrutinib could bring in over $4 billion in peak sales, if approved for patients with relapsing forms of MS.
The two competing MS drugs belong to a class of treatments previously linked to liver toxicity, making safety a closely watched concern.
While Roche's fenebrutinib could have an edge in terms of efficacy, it showed significantly higher liver enzyme elevations versus the comparator drug. Novartis said there was no liver safety signal in its drug.

items.title: Hugo Boss set to become Frasers subsidiary as stake crosses 50%
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Fashion group Hugo Boss will become a subsidiary of Mike Ashley-controlled Frasers after the British retailer on Friday raised its stake in the German company to more than 50%.
items.body:
Fashion group Hugo Boss (BOSSn.DE) will become a subsidiary of Mike Ashley-controlled Frasers (FRAS.L) after the British retailer on Friday raised its stake in the German company to more than 50%.
Frasers, which made a [USN:L6N43B0GF TEXT:"failed €2 billion takeover bid"] for the German fashion house in June, said it had bought a further 198,666 Hugo Boss shares for about €7.6 million ($8.51 million), taking its total stake to about 34.5 million shares, or 50.08%.
Hugo Boss' earnings, assets and liabilities are expected to be consolidated into Frasers' accounts as the stake passed 50%, the British firm said.
A Hugo Boss spokesperson said the company had taken note of Frasers' latest stake increase, but said that crossing the 50% threshold would not have any major implications.
Frasers, which has been pushing in to the premium and luxury space and ramping up its pursuit of the underperforming German designer known for its boxy men's suits, said crossing the 50% stake threshold was in the best interests of its investors.
Since Hugo Boss rejected a [USN:L6N43B0GF TEXT:"€38-per-share cash offer"] as "financially inadequate," the company's chairman has stepped down and Frasers CEO Michael Murray has become the chairman of its supervisory board while the British company has steadily raised its stake.
The stake purchase was funded from existing cash resources, Frasers said.
Frasers shares closed 0.3% higher on Friday, while Hugo Boss ended 0.8% lower.
($1 = 0.8935 euro)

items.title: Bears TE Cole Kmet (knee) to miss rest of season
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Chicago Bears tight end Cole Kmet is going on injured reserve with a season-ending knee injury, head coach Ben Johnson confirmed on Friday.
items.body:
Chicago Bears tight end Cole Kmet is going on injured reserve with a season-ending knee injury, head coach Ben Johnson confirmed on Friday.
Kmet was carted off the field in the fourth quarter of Thursday night's 30-24 home victory against the New England Patriots. He grabbed his right knee after being tackled low following an 8-yard catch and finished with three receptions for 28 yards.
"He's a big part of our heartbeat," Johnson said. "It stinks. I hate it."
Kmet, 27, had 10 receptions for 87 yards and one touchdown in seven games (three starts) this season. He has one season left on a four-year, $50 million contract extension signed in July 2023.
Drafted by Chicago in the second round out of Notre Dame in 2020, Kmet has collected 298 catches for 3,026 yards and 22 TDs in 107 career games (94 starts).
Johnson said Kmet's absence is an opportunity for 2026 third-round pick Sam Roush to step up. Roush, 23, has three catches for 33 yards in seven games this season for the Bears (5-2).
"We'll be able to see the player that we drafted," Johnson said. "We had high hopes when we took him. ... I'm confident in what he's going to be able to do for us back half of the season."
--Field Level Media

ホワイトハウスで記者団に対し、この問題についてスペースＸのイーロン・マスク最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）とは話していないが、利用上の問題が解消されなければ同氏と話すとし、「問題があるなら、私が解決する」と明言した。

items.title: 中国、宇宙での軍拡競争に反対　探査の権利保障訴え＝文書
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [北京 ２３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[北京 ２３日 ロイター] - 中国外務省は２３日、宇宙での軍拡競争に反対すると表明した。宇宙の探査や平和目的での利用を呼びかけ、すべての国による宇宙の探査や利用の権利が保障されるべきだと訴えている。

外務省が公表した宇宙を巡る中国政府の立場を記した文書によると、宇宙の「武器化」や軍事化のほか、「他国の主権や安全保障、開発上の利益を損なう活動」に利用することに反対し、「宇宙での軍拡競争リスクや戦場化しようとする動きが、宇宙の安全に対する最大の脅威と課題になっている」と言及した。中国は「宇宙の軍拡競争を防ぐためにあらゆる努力を払う」ことを求めていると説明している。

中国は商業的な宇宙活動の規制を求め、宇宙関連の経済の発展を奨励すると主張。商業的な宇宙活動は「他国の正当な権利や利益を侵害してはならず、武力紛争や内政に違法に介入することは避けるべきだ」とした。

[ワシントン ２３日 ロイター] - ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は２３日、ウクライナ、ロシア、米国の和平交渉担当者が、１１月前半にアラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）のアブダビで実務レベルの協議を開くことで合意したと明らかにした。その後に３カ国の首脳会談が行われることを期待していると述べた。

ゼレンスキー氏はシンクタンクのハドソン研究所にビデオリンクを通じて「計画では１１月前半、もちろんできるだけ早期に会合を開く予定だ」と語った。その上で、今月開催が見込まれていた同様の会合が実現しなかったことに言及し、多くはロシア次第であるとの見解を示した。 

その上で、実務協議の後に３カ国の首脳会談を開催することが極めて重要だと強調した。

ゼレンスキー氏は、ロシアのプーチン大統領と今週会談したトランプ大統領の娘婿クシュナー氏、ウィットコフ中東担当特使と２３日に協議を行ったと説明。和平合意にはウクライナに対する強力な安全保障の保証と、ウクライナ軍を維持するための１０年間の資金拠出が必要になるとの見方を示した。

Iran has detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables if war resumes, officials say

23 October, 2026 10:30 pm IST

DUBAI, Oct 23 (Reuters) – Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to target undersea communications cables in the Gulf if the United States and Israel attack Iran again, two senior Iranian security officials told Reuters.

Their comments followed warnings by Iranian officials that undersea cables in the region could become targets in any renewed conflict if diplomacy with Washington collapses.

The two Iranian security officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, gave few details and did not say how or where exactly Tehran would carry out such attacks. But one of them said Iran would aim to prevent repairs after any attacks to prolong disruptions to communications, including internet connections.

Show Full Article

“If Iran is attacked, there will be no more red lines … from undersea cables to military bases, including covert ones,” one of the officials said.

The official warned Washington not to “play with fire”, and said Iran had full access to the undersea cables and could easily destroy them.

Yadollah Javani, the deputy head of political affairs for Iran’s Revolutionary Guards (IRGC), said on Wednesday that Iran could target seven major internet cables beneath the Strait of Hormuz if Iranian infrastructure came under attack.

Undersea cables carry around 99% of global internet traffic, according to the International Telecommunication Union, a UN agency. But the global impact of such attacks by Iran could be limited as less than 1% of international bandwidth passes through the Strait of Hormuz, said Alan Mauldin, research director at telecommunications research firm TeleGeography.

The strait separates Iran and Oman, linking the Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea.

The US Department of State and Iran’s Foreign Ministry did not respond to Reuters’ requests for comment on the Iranian security officials’ remarks. There was no immediate comment from Gulf states.

‘STRONGER RESPONSE’

The plans for possible attacks on undersea cables reflect a conviction in Iran’s leadership that a renewed US military campaign would have to be met with a stronger response than before.

Top security official Mohsen Rezaei warned this month that US-linked digital infrastructure across the Gulf, including data centres and AI facilities, could be targeted in a renewed conflict.

Washington’s Gulf allies have invested heavily in such infrastructure and they “should hold Washington, not Tehran, responsible for any damage to undersea cables,” the second Iranian security official said.

Alex Vatanka, director of the Iran program at the Middle East Institute in Washington, said such threats were intended to deter renewed conflict and put pressure on Washington by making Gulf governments and US companies fear for their investments in the region.

“Tehran wants Gulf states and corporate executives to press (US President Donald) Trump over the risks his policies pose to their investment plans,” said Vatanka.

Multiple cable cuts could slow internet services and disrupt financial transactions, e-commerce and cloud computing, analysts said. The impact would depend on how operators rerouted traffic and the capacity available on alternative connections, Mauldin said.

Restoring connections during wartime could be difficult, experts said, and higher insurance costs and delays in obtaining permits to enter territorial waters could further complicate repairs.

The Red Sea could offer a more significant target than the Strait of Hormuz, particularly if Iran had support from its Houthi allies in Yemen, though Tehran has made no public statement indicating it plans to target cables there.

The Red Sea carries data between Europe, East Africa and Asia, with capacity routed through it accounting for about 3% of global international demand and around 10% of traffic travelling between regions, Mauldin said.

Gulf governments have been investing heavily in technology to diversify beyond oil and become global artificial intelligence hubs, deepening ties with US technology firms.

Iranian strikes directly hit two Amazon Web Services facilities in the UAE in March and damaged infrastructure near one of its facilities in Bahrain. The IRGC named US tech companies including Microsoft, Google, Apple and Nvidia as legitimate targets at the height of the war in March.

Land-based connections can provide alternative routes for internet traffic, and Gulf states and US technology companies are investing in additional infrastructure to improve resilience.

Microsoft plans to invest more than $400 million in subsea and terrestrial connectivity across the Middle East by 2030.

(Editing by Parisa Hafezi and Timothy Heritage)

NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 23 : Stock indexes were mixed on Friday, with tech shares edging higher after the previous day's selloff, while Brent crude oil rose to its highest in more than five months after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia.
The Nasdaq was up 0.2 per cent after starting the day lower, while the Dow was last down about 1 per cent.
An index of semiconductors was up about 1 per cent. It posted its biggest daily percentage drop since June on Thursday after a report from Meta Platforms reignited worries about the AI trade.
It's been "a very volatile week," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth in Boston.

"After Meta's report, there's still anxiety over the AI trade to a certain extent," he said. "But also, we continue to be in a place where things look like they're getting worse, not better, in the Middle East. That moves energy prices higher, which is obviously going to end up being a significant headwind for economic activity."
Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia fanned fears over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East, where United Arab Emirates authorities also reported an oil spill.
US crude rose 2.56 per cent to $102.02 a barrel and Brent climbed to $116.27 per barrel, up 2.74 per cent. European natural gas prices jumped. 
AMEX, TELECOM SHARES FALL
Investors were digesting corporate earnings news. American Express shares fell 3.5 per cent after it reported results and its CEO said the company had good momentum, but needed to become a more "agile and efficient" organization.
Telecom company shares, including Verizon, dropped after a Bloomberg News report that SpaceX was in talks with cellular infrastructure companies about launching a US wireless carrier program.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 476.25 points, or 0.9 per cent, to 52,391.73, the S&P 500 eased 11.14 points, or 0.14 per cent, to 7,652.96 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 52.51 points, or 0.21 per cent, to 26,062.75.
MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 1.64 points, or 0.15 per cent, to 1,121.29.The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.4 per cent.
Asia's bourses steadied overnight, with South Korea's KOSPI ending its session higher after shedding as much as 4 per cent earlier.
US Treasury yields rose a day after the benchmark 10-year yield registered its biggest one-day drop in nearly four years, but remained under 5 per cent.
The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was last up 3.7 basis points at 4.992 per cent. The 10-year yield is down about 11 basis points on the week and on pace for a third straight week of declines, its longest run lower since June.
EURO FALLS
The euro fell and was on track for a weekly loss against both the US dollar and the yen, while euro zone bonds stabilized after recent volatility. Investors' focus has been on concerns over France's finances.
French yields, which were down 5 basis points at 5.04 per cent, have risen nearly 27 bps this week, the most of any major euro zone country and the most in a week since late May. 
A selloff in French government bonds this week pushed the country's debt risk premium to its highest level since the euro zone sovereign debt crisis in 2011.
France will deploy 70,000 police backed by specialist units for protests on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said. The country faces the threat of a rating downgrade by Moody’s later on Friday.
The euro was last down 0.12 per cent at $1.12, set to end the week 0.35 per cent lower. 

Source: Reuters

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 476.25 points, or 0.9 per cent, to 52,391.73, the S&P 500 eased 11.14 points, or 0.14 per cent, to 7,652.96 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 52.51 points, or 0.21 per cent, to 26,062.75.
MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 1.64 points, or 0.15 per cent, to 1,121.29.The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 0.4 per cent.
Asia's bourses steadied overnight, with South Korea's KOSPI ending its session higher after shedding as much as 4 per cent earlier.
US Treasury yields rose a day after the benchmark 10-year yield registered its biggest one-day drop in nearly four years, but remained under 5 per cent.
The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was last up 3.7 basis points at 4.992 per cent. The 10-year yield is down about 11 basis points on the week and on pace for a third straight week of declines, its longest run lower since June.
EURO FALLS
The euro fell and was on track for a weekly loss against both the US dollar and the yen, while euro zone bonds stabilized after recent volatility. Investors' focus has been on concerns over France's finances.
French yields, which were down 5 basis points at 5.04 per cent, have risen nearly 27 bps this week, the most of any major euro zone country and the most in a week since late May. 
A selloff in French government bonds this week pushed the country's debt risk premium to its highest level since the euro zone sovereign debt crisis in 2011.
France will deploy 70,000 police backed by specialist units for protests on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said. The country faces the threat of a rating downgrade by Moody’s later on Friday.
The euro was last down 0.12 per cent at $1.12, set to end the week 0.35 per cent lower. 

Source: Reuters

Oct 23 : US telecom stocks declined on Friday after a report that SpaceX was seeking thousands of cell sites for a fourth wireless carrier, fueling concerns over fresh competition.
Elon Musk's rocket and space technology company was in talks to access at least 80,000 cell sites to build its wireless carrier from scratch, Bloomberg News reported late on Thursday, citing sources familiar with the matter.
AT&T fell 5.6 per cent to a more than three-month low, Verizon lost 1.6 per cent and T-Mobile shed 5 per cent. 
Germany's Deutsche Telekom, which holds an over 50 per cent stake in T-Mobile, lost 3.2 per cent.

"The competitive impact may still be years away, but anticipation alone, reinforced by each successive spectrum and infrastructure move, is likely to remain an overhang on sector sentiment," Bernstein analysts said in a note.
Tower operators and SpaceX did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
The report comes weeks after SpaceX acquired low-band spectrum to advance its carrier plans, mounting a direct, orbital challenge to legacy wireless giants in the US and sending AT&T and Verizon shares to their worst one-day falls in more than two decades.
Bernstein analysts said that an MVNO (mobile virtual network operator) deal with SpaceX may not appeal to telecom operators, but a unified stance against one has done little to lift sentiment, leaving carriers to reassess their options.
SpaceX's Starlink has been generating revenue from internet services in sparsely populated and rural areas, but becoming a true rival to major carriers will require years of work and a terrestrial network.
Tower operator Crown Castle, however, surged 11.6 per cent after the report identified it as one of the cellular infrastructure companies SpaceX was in talks with. 
Other operators also rose, with American Tower up 4.9 per cent and SBA Communications adding 4.6 per cent. 
Shares of SpaceX rose 1.7 per cent.

items.title: Trump and Burnham discuss North Sea oil, Ukraine and Falklands
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: US President Donald Trump said he discussed opening up North Sea oil during a conversation with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, as well as touching on the conflicts in Iran and Ukraine "very lightly."
items.body:
US President Donald Trump said he discussed opening up North Sea oil during a conversation with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, as well as touching on the conflicts in Iran and Ukraine "very lightly."
"They're opening up the North Sea oil," Trump told reporters at the White House before departing for a campaign trip to Florida ahead of the November 3 midterm US elections. "I've been after them to do that for two years... Andy is getting it done."
On Wednesday, Trump praised Britain's approval of the [USN:L8N46707X TEXT:"Jackdaw North Sea gas field"], a decision that ended years of legal and political wrangling, though British officials said a decision about the bigger Rosebank oilfield was yet to be made.
Burnham's office said in a statement that the two leaders agreed the Jackdaw approval would bring "significant benefits" to Britain. They also welcomed continued cooperation between British and US companies, particularly on nuclear power.
Burnham also raised the topic of oil exploration off the [USN:L6N45F0WA TEXT:"Falkland Islands,"] a largely self-governing British overseas territory whose sovereignty Argentina has long disputed. Burnham spoke about the economic consequences for Britain and the US of what he described as Argentina's coercive [USN:S0N44M029 TEXT:"measures"] seeking to halt the drilling and reiterated the importance of respecting the islanders' right to develop their natural resources, Downing Street added.
On Ukraine, Burnham underlined the importance of Kyiv having full access to [USN:L6N4690ZQ TEXT:"Starlink"] to defend itself against Russia and welcomed Trump's efforts to bring Russian President Vladimir Putin to the negotiating table. The leaders agreed to work with international partners to end the bloodshed, the statement said.
The leaders also discussed the Middle East, with Burnham reaffirming Britain's support for Saudi Arabia in the face of [USN:L1N46809Q TEXT:"Houthi attacks"].

Oct 23 : PwC on Friday said it was aware of a cybersecurity incident involving a third-party vendor used to host company employee learning records, the day after a cyber extortion group claimed to have stolen 590 gigabytes of company data.
• A PwC global spokesperson said "the affected site does not house client data, sensitive personal data or financial information. Once we learned of this incident we acted promptly to secure the environment and conduct a thorough review."
• The incident "does not impact our network or any of our operations," the spokesperson said.
• A cyber extortion group called "Everest" claimed responsibility for the data breach in a message posted to its website October 22, according to cybercrime research platform eCrime.ch. The message included a countdown timer with five days remaining, and a message indicating the data would be released if a deal could not be reached.

items.title: Rendimientos EEUU suben ligeramente, título a 10 años sigue por debajo 5% ante nerviosismo por IA
items.author: Chuck Mikolajczak
items.creator: Chuck Mikolajczak
items.summary: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos subieron el viernes, un día después de que el rendimiento de referencia a 10 años registrara su mayor caída diaria en casi cuatro años, aunque se mantenían bajo el umbral del 5% debido a la persistente preocupación por la sostenibilidad del repunte de las acciones relacionadas con la IA.
items.body:
Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos subieron el viernes, un día después de que el rendimiento de referencia a 10 años registrara su mayor caída diaria en casi cuatro años, aunque se mantenían bajo el umbral del 5% debido a la persistente preocupación por la sostenibilidad del repunte de las acciones relacionadas con la IA.
*El rendimiento del bono del Tesoro estadounidense a 10 años de referencia subió 3,7 puntos básicos, hasta el 4,99%. El rendimiento a 10 años ha bajado unos 11 puntos básicos en la semana y va camino de registrar su tercera semana consecutiva de descensos, su racha bajista más larga desde junio.
*Los inversionistas se han decantado por activos más seguros, como la deuda pública, ante las recientes preocupaciones sobre la sostenibilidad de la tendencia alcista de la IA, un componente clave del actual mercado de la renta variable. El reciente repunte del mercado de bonos se ha producido a pesar de que los datos económicos apuntan a presiones continuadas sobre los precios y de que el petróleo ha superado los 100 dólares por barril.
*Sin embargo, mientras que el sector tecnológico del S&P 500 (.SPLRCT) subió a medida que se disipaban los temores sobre la IA, el índice S&P 500 en su conjunto (.SPX) retrocedió.
*El rendimiento de los bonos a 10 años se desplomó 19,3 puntos básicos el jueves, su mayor caída desde el 10 de marzo de 2023, cuando las autoridades reguladoras cerraron SVB Financial Group tras el fallido intento del banco de obtener capital.
*"Volveremos a ver rendimientos superiores al 5% para el bono a 10 años. No estamos tan lejos, pero tampoco es como para decir: “Oh, vale, ya estamos en plena carrera”", afirmó JoAnne Bianco, socia y estratega senior de inversiones de BondBloxx Investment Management en Chicago.
*"Sigue habiendo muchos factores adversos, como la inflación persistente, la creciente oferta de bonos del Tesoro para financiar los déficits, la necesidad general —con toda la incertidumbre que ello conlleva— de primas de plazo más elevadas y, además, los precios más altos de la energía, que parecen que van a mantenerse durante un tiempo".
*El rendimiento del bono a 30 años subió 2,9 puntos básicos hasta el 5,316%, pero bajó casi 13 puntos básicos en la semana, encaminándose además hacia su tercera semana consecutiva de descensos.
*A pesar de que los datos económicos apuntan a un aumento de las presiones sobre los precios, las expectativas del mercado respecto a una subida de tasas por parte de la Reserva Federal en su reunión de política monetaria de la próxima semana se han desvanecido. La probabilidad de una subida de al menos 25 puntos básicos se ha reducido al 9,4%, según el CME FedWatch, desde el 15,5% de hace una semana y el 70,9% de hace un mes.
*Un indicador muy seguido de la curva de rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos, que mide la diferencia entre los rendimientos de los bonos a 2 y a 10 años —y que se considera un indicador de las expectativas económicas—, se situó en 29,6 puntos básicos positivos.
*El rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a dos años , que suele evolucionar en consonancia con las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés de la Fed, subió 5,5 puntos básicos hasta el 4,69%, lo que supone un descenso de unos 5 puntos básicos en la semana, lo que representaría la cuarta semana consecutiva de caídas, su racha más larga del año.
*La tasa de equilibrio de los Títulos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos protegidos contra la inflación (TIPS) a 5 años se situó por última vez en el 2,456%, en camino de alcanzar su cierre más alto desde el 10 de septiembre, tras cerrar el jueves en el 2,38%.
*La tasa de equilibrio de los TIPS a 10 años se situaba en el 2,346%, lo que indica que el mercado prevé una inflación media de alrededor del 2,3% anual durante la próxima década.
